description:
FILED s470bx (Opus, 2026-09-06) by the #1043 emission A/B: t/op/stat.t:459 was
one of the five movers, and probing WHY turned up a PRE-EXISTING gap that has
nothing to do with stat.

THE SHAPE.  `\` distributes over a LIST, and a function CALL that returns a
list is such a list â perlref, and perl's own regression for bug id
20011101.069 (t/op/stat.t:459) is exactly this:

    my @r = \stat($Curdir);
    is(scalar @r, 13,   'stat returns full 13 elements');

PROBED 5.40.3 vs PCL (scratch/s470bx/pbs.pl), perl / PCL:

    my @r = \stat(".")        13 refs (SCALAR)  /  1 ref
    my @l = \localtime(0)      9 refs           /  1 ref
    sub three { (7,8,9) }
    my @c = \three()           3 refs           /  1 ref
    my @b = \(@a)              3 refs           /  3 refs   OK
    my @d = \(1,2)             2 refs           /  2 refs   OK

So the SLICE/range spread shipped by #892 (`_is_refgen_spread_node` â the
range operator plus the four slice node types) is right as far as it goes; a
CALL is simply not in the predicate, and neither is a list-returning builtin.

WHERE IT SITS.  Two things are wrong together and they must be fixed together:

  (1) the refgen OPERAND is annotated SCALAR context, so a wantarray-sensitive
      builtin in that slot is emitted wrapped:
        `\localtime(0)`  ->  (p-backslash (p-scalar-ctx (p-localtime 0)))
      â measured on the fcf076f1 tree, i.e. BEFORE #1043, so this is the
      long-standing annotation for every member of %WANTARRAY_SENSITIVE
      (localtime, gmtime, caller, each, splice, readdir, unpack, reverse, â¦).
  (2) `p-backslash` would then have to SPREAD over the list it receives, the
      way `_is_refgen_spread_node` already makes it spread over a slice.

Fixing (2) without (1) buys nothing (the operand is already collapsed to one
value before p-backslash sees it); fixing (1) without (2) makes the operand a
13-element vector that p-backslash wraps in ONE ref, which is what the base
tree did.

WHAT #1043 CHANGED, AND WHAT IT DID NOT.  Adding `stat`/`lstat` to
%WANTARRAY_SENSITIVE made `\stat(...)` join its siblings: the count was 1
before and is 1 after, so no assertion moves, but the ONE ref is now a SCALAR
ref to 1 instead of an ARRAY ref to the 13-element vector.  t/op/stat.t's row
fails on both trees for the same reason (and that file produces ZERO rows
today anyway â #1232).  No sweep, companion or gate row moves; verified by the
#1043 full sweep and by op/stat.t / op/filetest.t / op/stat_errors.t companion
legs.

FIX SHAPE (untried): widen the predicate that decides a refgen SPREAD to
include a call whose return is a list, annotate that operand LIST, and make
`p-backslash` map over a vector operand when the spread licence is present.
The acceptance table is the five-row probe above, plus the four #892 negatives
(`\(@A,$x)` is (ARRAY, SCALAR), `\(@A,@B)` is (ARRAY, ARRAY)) which must NOT
start spreading.
subject: `\FUNC(...)` does not spread over the returned LIST â the refgen operand is annotated SCALAR and p-backslash wraps once (t/op/stat.t:459, bug id 20011101.069)
